paper_role: Zero-shot REM-Net representation gate; calibration experiments remain supplementary only
hypothesis: Signed native-rate RCG is useful only when treated as a standardized phase residual conditioned on stable WSST context; naive fusion lets subject-specific phase dominate and does not generalize.
protocol: MMECG loso_v2 folds 5/9, train and validation only, held-out ECG used only for validation metrics, no calibration, test unopened

arms.P0-naive: WSST semantic stream plus per-window/per-bin standardized signed RCG residual, with unit fusion gate
arms.P1-gated: parameter-identical streams and decoder; WSST-RCG interaction predicts the phase-residual gate

parity: P0 and P1 instantiate identical parameters, optimizer, loss, budget, seed, preprocessing, decoder, checkpoint rule and evaluator; only the forward use of the already-instantiated gate differs
output: continuous ECG [B,1,1600] at 200 Hz under train-fold robust scaling
budget: 80 epochs, patience 20, AdamW lr=1e-4 weight_decay=1e-4, batch 16, effective seed=42+fold
gate: P1 exceeds P0 and repaired B1 on both folds 5 and 9; fold-macro PCC gain over B1 >=0.10; R2 also improves on both folds
failure_rule: If the gate fails, terminate phase-fusion scaling and move to population morphology/event formulation without a broader fusion sweep
